newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva bank ups cash exposure, cautious on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Geneva bank ups cash exposure, cautious on stocks.

text.p: Bordier & Cie, one of Geneva's oldest private banks founded in 1844, is increasing its cash holdings at the expense of stocks and cutting exposure to the Swiss franc, its first vice-president Michel Juvet said.
He said the bank was wary of low returns on world equity markets and also switching to shorter-term maturities in bonds.
"Globally, we feel uncomfortable. It is a very boring environment, nothing is particularly attractive," he said.

The bank, which does not publish the volume of assets it manages, has 32.5 percent of its portfolio in cash, 25 percent in bonds, 22 percent in shares, 15 percent in other instruments and five percent in warrants and call options which it has been using since November to play in equity indices.
In emerging markets, Juvet said the bank's portfolio weighing was neutral in Hong Kong where shares were becoming expensive.
He said the bank had no exposure to emerging markets in Eastern Europe, Latin America and Russia, which bankers expect to rally in 1997 on U.S. cash seeking higher returns abroad.
The majority of the bank's equity exposure is in Europe and that of bonds in Switzerland, Juvet said.
In currency terms, Bordier & Cie is keeping a weak exposure to the Swiss Franc in favour of the dollar, he added.
A run from the mark and other European currencies drove the Swiss franc sharply higher in 1995, but the currency began easing to more normal levels last year and has continued this trend into 1997.
Private banks in Switzerland manage an estimated $1.8 trillion in assets, according to a recent survey by Credit Suisse First Boston Bank (CSFB).
The survey says Swiss private asset management grew 13 percent on average a year in 1990-1995 with commission income up 11 percent annually.
Annual growth at Swiss private banking business should slow down to 10 percent for assets and eight percent for commissions in the coming years amid growing competition, it added.
